data.name: Maheshwar
data.gender_notes: Maheshwar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Maheshwar is a name derived from Sanskrit language, which means 'God of Gods'. This name is associated with Lord Shiva, who is the supreme deity in Hinduism. Maheshwar is believed to symbolize power, strength, and wisdom. The name Maheshwar carries the meaning “God of Gods” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Maheshwar usually hope their child will grow to embody god of gods and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the supreme power and wisdom of Lord Shiva.
data.etymology: Maheshwar belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Gods.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Maheshwar total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

vedic_reference.note: Maheshwar is a name of Lord Shiva, the supreme god in Hinduism. He is also known as Mahadeva, the great god.

historical_references.reference: Maheshwar was an important Hindu pilgrimage site during the medieval period, particularly for the Kalchuri dynasty. The town is named after the god Mahadeva, or Shiva, and is situated on the banks of the Narmada River.
historical_references.context: Medieval Hindu religious site and capital city of the Kalchuri kingdom

historical_references.reference: Maheshwar was an ancient Hindu trading centre and prospered as a significant political centre during the 6th century CE when it was the capital of the Malava kingdom. The name Maheshwar is derived from the god Mahesvara, or Shiva, and the city was known for its famous Shiva temple.
